summary: Capacity mining of PR #408 exact head d31c100c5d3766ca14d89b046fff4cdb09086754 found that assertCanonicalRecipe exact-validates WorldEntity record/origin keys but does not close the outer PhysicsLabRecipe shapes. The top-level recipe accepts unknown fields; the entities table is checked only by # and ipairs so extra map/non-array entries are ignored; and each primitive/object entity-recipe table is accepted without an exact allowed-key fence. This is a source-contract gap in the retained canonical-recipe constructor boundary. The active independent synthesis reviewer should decide whether to REQUEST_CHANGES; if repaired, add bounded regressions for extra top-level fields, extra entity-list map entries, and unknown entity-recipe fields without widening runtime architecture.
evidence: PR #408 exact source head d31c100c5d3766ca14d89b046fff4cdb09086754 defines exact RECORD_KEYS and ORIGIN_KEYS fences, but assertCanonicalRecipe performs no equivalent exact-key validation on recipeTable or entityRecipe.

The same function accepts entities after assertPlainTable plus #entities == canonical count, then iterates with ipairs; a plain table containing the canonical dense array plus an extra map key is therefore outside the canonical recipe shape yet is not inspected by that loop.

PhysicsLabRecipe defines distinct fixed primitive/object recipe records with geometry/material/ObjectGenome fields, so the missing outer-shape fence is not an intentionally open arbitrary-map contract.

Current PhysicsLabRealizer builds PhysicsLabRecipe internally before constructing the runtime, so this source finding does not claim a demonstrated current Workspace divergence or engine exploit; it concerns the public runtime constructor contract and future adapter safety.
No code was changed, no executable test was run, and no Roblox Studio, viewport, contact, or two-client evidence is claimed by this mining result.
